definitions.title: Method of Lagrange Multipliers (One Constraint)
definitions.latex: \nabla f = \lambda \nabla g, \quad g(x, y, z) = k
definitions.statement: To find the maximum and minimum values of f(x, y, z) subject to constraint g(x, y, z) = k (assuming grad g != 0 on the constraint surface), find all values of x, y, z and scalar multiplier lambda satisfying grad f = lambda grad g alongside g = k.
conditions: grad g != 0 on the level surface g = k
f and g have continuous partials
definitions.explanation: At an extremum, the level surface of f must be tangent to the constraint surface g = k, meaning their normal gradient vectors must be parallel.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Transforms constrained optimization into an unconstrained system of equations.

definitions.title: Lagrange Multipliers with Two Constraints
definitions.latex:
abla f = \lambda 
abla g + \mu 
abla h, \quad g = k_1, \; h = k_2
definitions.statement: To optimize f subject to two simultaneous constraints g = k_1 and h = k_2, the gradient of f must lie in the plane spanned by the constraint gradients grad g and grad h.
conditions: grad g and grad h are linearly independent
definitions.explanation: The curve of intersection of the two constraint surfaces is orthogonal to grad f at the extremum point.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Optimizes functions along space curves formed by intersecting surfaces.
